summary: The week's reading centers on Psalms that call all creation to praise the Lord, highlighting His enduring mercy, faithfulness, and power. It includes prayers of the afflicted, messianic prophecies about Jesus Christ, blessings for those who fear God, and the sustaining role of God's word as a guide. The selections invite personal reflection on suffering, trust in God's eternal nature, and joyful worship.

background: The Psalms (Tehillim) are a collection of sacred songs and poems used in ancient Israelite worship, many attributed to King David. They express a wide range of human emotions—praise, lament, trust—and were sung in the temple and synagogues. The collection continues to be central in Jewish and Christian worship, inviting believers to acknowledge God's power, mercy, and faithfulness.

manualHighlights.note: The week's theme is 'Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise the Lord,' emphasizing praise as a response to God's power and mercy.
Psalms 102–103 and 116 show how the Lord comforts us in suffering and invites us to call upon His name.
Psalms 110 and 118 contain messianic prophecies fulfilled by Jesus Christ, such as His sitting at God's right hand and being the cornerstone.
Psalm 119 teaches that God's word is a lamp to our feet and a light to our path, helping us stay on the way to Heavenly Father.
Psalms 135–136 contrast the Lord's power with the impotence of idols, reminding us to trust in the true God.
Psalm 139 reveals that the Lord knows our thoughts, actions, and innermost being, encouraging personal accountability and trust.
